title: Carpio: Political dynasties feed on national budget
summary: Political dynasties have been “feeding on the budget” passed by Congress every year, and there is a need to remove them, according to retired Supreme Court senior associate justice…

blocks.text: Retired Supreme Court justice Antonio Carpio warned.

MANILA, Philippines — Political dynasties have been “feeding on the budget” passed by Congress every year, and there is a need to remove them, according to retired Supreme Court senior associate justice Antonio Carpio.

Between 75 and 85 percent of the current members of the Senate and the House of Representatives belong to political dynasties, Carpio said. He noted that the number has ballooned since the ratification of the 1987 Constitution.

“That used to be 20 percent in 1987. How come they have grown so huge? They have intensified their control,” he said during an interview in a YouTube podcast hosted by content creator Carlo Ople on Tuesday.

Carpio said the people can fight back against political dynasties by joining an online campaign aimed at collecting signatures to be able to enact an anti-political dynasty law without approval from Congress.

With Congress enacting the General Appropriations Act (GAA) or the national budget every year, Carpio stressed that members of political dynasties in the two chambers are able to insert fund allocations or pork barrel, including the Priority Development Assistance Fund (PDAF) that has been declared unconstitutional.

This time, members of political dynasties in Congress make way for fund allocations by allotting them to flood control projects for instance, wherein 70 percent of the funds are “wasted,” he noted.?Caprio cited testimonies by former Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) undersecretary Roberto Bernardo that up to 25 percent of funds of flood control projects went to some lawmakers as kickbacks.

“How did the political dynasties grow? How did they come to dominate everything? Because of the money in the budget. Every year, they use that to buy votes. Therefore, the political dynasties feed on the budget every year… to perpetuate themselves and to enlarge themselves in power,” he said.

As political dynasties remain prevalent, coupled with high inflation rate currently at 7.8 percent and weak confidence of investors in the country due to corruption issues, Carpio warned the public might get fed up and launch a revolution similar to the riots in France and Italy since last month.
“It won’t take long and it will happen to us. So we have to prepare for that because if we have rioting, everybody suffers,” he warned.

Carpio is currently one of the convenors of the Dapat Isa Lang Movement, which would gather signatures of registered voters from three percent of each of the country’s 254 legislative districts or 10 percent of registered voters nationwide.

The proposed law would require that only one member of the family up to the fourth degree of relationship, also applicable to spouses and his or her family members, will seek each national and local elective public office.
It could be passed into law through a people’s initiative, without relying on the approval of Congress, according to Carpio.

Meanwhile, Caloocan Rep. Edgar Erice urged the Senate to look at congressional insertions in the proposed P7.2-trillion national budget for 2027 as red flags which deserve further scrutiny. — Daphne Galvez
